hints: Think about what harmful pollutants are actually made inside a petrol engine from incomplete burning and high temperatures.
Remember that CO and unburnt hydrocarbons come from incomplete combustion, while NOx forms when nitrogen and oxygen react in the hot engine.
Ask yourself which gases are harmless products like CO2 that we want to make, and which gases like SO2 are not dealt with by the converter.
walkthrough:
**Recall what comes out of the engine**

Petrol does not burn perfectly. This gives toxic $\text{CO}$ and unburnt $\text{hydrocarbons}$. The very high temperature also lets nitrogen and oxygen from air react to make $\text{NO}_x$.

These three are the main harmful exhaust pollutants.

**Recall what the converter does**

The converter uses Pt, Pd and Rh catalysts to do two jobs at once. It oxidises toxic gases to harmless ones, and reduces nitrogen oxides back to nitrogen.

Key reactions:
$$2\text{CO} + 2\text{NO} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + \text{N}_2$$
$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y + (x + y/4)\text{O}_2 \rightarrow x\text{CO}_2 + (y/2)\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Pick the correct trio**

So the gases removed (used up) are carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides. They are converted into harmless $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{N}_2$.

options.A: Correct. CO is oxidised to CO2, unburnt hydrocarbons are oxidised to CO2 and H2O, and NOx is reduced to N2. These are the three classic pollutants targeted by the three-way catalytic converter.
options.B: Incorrect. Carbon dioxide is not removed, it is produced. The converter makes CO2 as a harmless product from oxidising CO and hydrocarbons.
options.C: Incorrect. Sulfur dioxide is not one of the three main gases removed. Modern low-sulfur petrol produces very little SO2, and it is not converted in the same way as CO and NOx.
options.D: Incorrect. While hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides are correct, sulfur dioxide is wrong. The missing gas should be carbon monoxide, the key toxic product of incomplete combustion.
